name: illustrator-quiz-board-multiline
exporter: Adobe Illustrator 2024 (28.6) - Export As > SVG, Styling: Internal CSS
story: A full-frame studio quiz board: the designer typed the question as one text object with two hard returns, so Illustrator wrote three stacked <tspan> lines (same x, y stepping 0/62/124) inside a single <text id="Question">, with four answer pills below. I claim the LINES THEY DREW - three question fields, not one block - because docs/SVG_AUTHORING.md section 3 states it without condition: a <text> with several positioned <tspan> lines becomes one field per line, each separately editable. The designer would probably rather have one wrapping question box, and the gap between what they want and what the page promises is exactly what this fixture exists to expose.
idioms: Generator comment naming the SVG Export Plug-In build
root attrs in Illustrator's order with x="0px" y="0px", viewBox/width/height and xml:space="preserve" on tab-indented continuation lines
<style type="text/css"> as a direct child of <svg>, one property per .stN class, uppercase hex
multiline point type as one <text transform="matrix(...)"> holding tspans with x="0" and y="0"/"62"/"124" - the leading baked into y, no dy
tspans written with no whitespace between them so no stray text nodes appear between lines
_x20_ escapes with data-name holding the original spelling on every answer row and on the card group
<rect y="0" ...> with the zero x omitted on the full-frame backplate
tab indentation, one tab per nesting level
whyThisMatters: Stacked tspans and kerned-run tspans are byte-identical apart from whether y varies, so an importer that gets this rule wrong fails one of the two files every time - and a quiz board is the graphic the 2026-09-12 production has to ship, where the wrong answer is either three unusable question boxes or one box that silently drops two thirds of the question.
